# Compressed joint cap stress and transport to deepest fibers

This strengthens `candidate 21a9da879344205f` by allowing the cap integer
normals and thresholds to vary together with the compatible fiber bodies.
It retains the projected coverage constraints explicitly. It does not assume
that arbitrary changes of a compressed cover preserve its covering property.

Work at an attained bounded-facet depth minimizer with all fibers positive,
as supplied by the alternative in `candidate 21db6cba533d25dc`.
Write its mass as M and its maximum normalized depth as beta>0.

## 1. At most 2^n relevant circuit groups, plus slack groups

For each integer fiber take a minimal positive continuous-normal circuit of
its active caps at its restricted maximizer, as proved in
`candidate b989614dc4f86228`. Write group i as

    H_ij={v_ij.z+u_ij.x>=b_ij},
    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0, rho_ij>0, sum_j rho_ij=1,

with k_i<=d+1 and rank k_i-1. At its own anchor (z_i,x_i), every cap plane
passes through that point. Thus, putting

    A_i=sum_j rho_ij v_ij,     h_i=sum_j rho_ij b_ij,

one has h_i=A_i.z_i. The projected closed halfspace

    G_i={z:A_i.z>=h_i}

contains its anchor z_i. Wherever G_i holds, the weighted sum of all the
ambient cap margins is nonnegative independently of x, so the group's closed
caps cover the ENTIRE continuous fiber. If A_i=0, its own-contact equation
also gives h_i=0 and this group covers every fiber.

The G_i cover P. By the finite-P form of Doignon's theorem, at most 2^n of
these groups suffice to cover P: replace each open complement by a closed
halfspace with the same trace on finite P, intersect with conv(P), and apply
the integer Helly theorem. This argument selects whole circuit groups.

Call a fiber deepest when its restricted maximum equals beta. A group
originating at a nondeep fiber has every cap mass STRICTLY below beta M.
It cannot cover an entire deepest fiber. Consequently the selected deepest
origin groups, at most 2^n of them, cover all deepest integer indices through
their projected G_i.

Now ADD the original local circuit group of every nondeep fiber; all these
added cap budgets are slack. Assign each deepest p to one selected group
with p in G_i, and assign each nondeep p to its own added group. This gives
one fixed assignment i(p) of all P. No count is needed for the added slack
groups because their first-order cap multipliers will be zero.

## 2. The joint variational problem has linear coverage constraints

Keep each u_ij and rho_ij fixed, but allow EVERY v_ij and b_ij to vary freely.
For each assigned p impose the linear inequality

    C_ip(v,b)=sum_j rho_ij(v_ij.p-b_ij)>=0.

These constraints ensure that the corresponding circuit covers the entire
fiber above p, regardless of the new fiber shape. They are homogeneous in
(v,b). The fiber-support compatibility constraints are homogeneous as well.

The given family and cap parameters globally maximize total volume among
competitors in the same bounded-facet class satisfying these coverage
constraints and every cap budget mu(H_ij)<=beta M. A larger-volume feasible
competitor would have depth strictly below beta because the assigned cap
groups still cover P x R^d.

Use the restricted individual-fan compatible support cone from
`candidate 21db6cba533d25dc`, Section 3: each fiber remains linear
on its own small-erosion normal fan, expressed on a common refinement. This
restriction preserves its original facet normals and its facet budget; an
unrestricted refinement cone is not being used.
Common fiber erosion changes neither v nor b, preserves all coverage
constraints, and strictly decreases every active cap-gradient possibility.
Thus the same separation argument gives a normalized objective stress with
nonnegative cap multipliers lambda_ij, nonnegative active coverage
multipliers eta_ip, and nonnegative compatibility multipliers. The cap
multipliers of all slack groups are zero.

The cap derivative formula has the SAME boundary trace coefficients in its
shape and cap-parameter parts. If s_ijz is the effective section area defined
in `candidate 21a9da879344205f`, the extra terms are

    + delta v_ij . sum_z s_ijz z
    - delta b_ij   sum_z s_ijz.

At a coincident facet this is verified by the relative swept-prism formula.
For a body lying inside the cap the contribution is the minimum of the body
facet-motion term and the cap-plane-motion term; for a body lying outside
it is their positive difference. The two possible linear pieces produce
exactly the earlier theta in [0,1] and the corresponding effective section
area s. Hence no new inconsistent choice of boundary weights is introduced.

## 3. Exact group transport equations

Put S_ij=sum_z s_ijz. It is strictly positive for any cap in a deepest-origin
group, because that cap passes through the interior of its own full-dimensional
anchor fiber. Stationarity in the FREE threshold b_ij gives

    lambda_ij S_ij = rho_ij t_i,
    t_i := sum_(p assigned to i) eta_ip.

Stationarity in its FREE integer normal v_ij gives

    lambda_ij sum_z s_ijz z
        = rho_ij sum_(p assigned to i) eta_ip p.

The eta are supported only on active coverage equalities C_ip=0. These
formulae have several exact consequences.

* In a group with t_i>0, every lambda_ij is positive and
  lambda_ij=t_i rho_ij/S_ij.
* In a deepest-origin group with t_i=0, all its cap multipliers are zero.
* Every slack group has lambda=0, and the threshold equation then forces
  eta=0 as well. In particular nondeep assigned points carry no transport
  stress.
* All caps of a nonzero group have the SAME section-marginal barycenter

      bar_z_i = sum_z s_ijz z / S_ij
              = sum_p eta_ip p / t_i.

  This is a convex combination of assigned GLOBAL DEEPEST integer fibers.
* Since each stressed coverage constraint is active,
  A_i.bar_z_i=h_i. The transported barycenter is on the group's projected
  boundary. It need not be an integer and is not claimed to be a center in S.

Only the at most 2^n selected deepest-origin groups can carry nonzero stress.
The count has therefore been retained without discarding the coverage
constraints or falsely treating the compressed cap normals as free.

## 4. Common contact with the transported deepest points

Every critical cap of mass beta M has every globally deepest point in its
closed complementary halfspace. If it contained one such point strictly,
move its boundary inward through that point. Its positive-volume fiber has
an interior ball, so the removed strip has positive mass, producing a
containing cap of mass less than beta M, a contradiction.

Let p be ANY assigned deepest index, and choose any globally deepest center
(p,x_p) in its fiber. Every cap margin in group i is nonpositive there, while
the covering assignment says their positive weighted sum C_ip is nonnegative.
Consequently C_ip=0 and EACH margin is zero. Thus every deepest assigned
index already has an active coverage equality and common cap contact, even
before requiring eta_ip>0.

Consequently the convex combination

    ybar_i = sum_p (eta_ip/t_i)(p,x_p)

belongs to C, has depth at least beta by convexity of depth regions, and lies
on every cap plane of group i. Its integer projection is bar_z_i. This is an
actual contact constructed from deepest points; it is not a replacement
mixed-integer candidate unless its projection happens to be integer.

## 5. The signed Euler offsets cancel exactly

For a nonzero group,

    sum_(j,z) lambda_ij (b_ij-v_ij.z) s_ijz
       = t_i sum_j rho_ij(b_ij-v_ij.bar_z_i)
       = t_i(h_i-A_i.bar_z_i)=0.

Thus the signed offset term in the earlier global Euler equation vanishes.
All active cap masses are beta M, so

    sum_(i,j) lambda_ij = 1/beta.

An equivalent direct check uses joint homothety: dilate all continuous
fibers by a factor q and replace every (v_ij,b_ij) by (qv_ij,qb_ij), leaving
u fixed. Every cap mass and total volume scale by q^d, and every active
homogeneous compatibility and coverage constraint stays zero. Evaluating
the objective stress on this direction gives the same identity, including
all boundary traces.

Combining the equations reduces the cap multipliers to the group data

    1/beta = sum_(nonzero i) t_i sum_j rho_ij/S_ij,
    number of nonzero groups <= 2^n.

No bound t_i sum_j rho_ij/S_ij <= 1/gamma_d has been proved here. In
particular, the transport and exact normalization are established facts;
the missing per-group estimate is not being asserted as a lemma.
